messages:
sara: Heads-up 1 — we have two enterprise prospects insisting on deterministic tail SLOs for critical routes and an automatic model fallback chain if the primary can't meet it. Competitor announcement this morning added urgency. Discuss parity vs differentiation?

alex: Clarifying Q 1: are they asking for an atomic, single-request guarantee (i.e., the request finishes within SLO on whichever model served) or are they ok with a best-effort attempt + async retry? Sales says single-call guarantee.

mohit: confirmed from Sales. They need "single-call graceful degrade" so the app doesn't have to orchestrate retries. They outlined chain: high-quality -> quantized variant -> smaller model.

julia: infra implications: synchronous fallback affects batching and KV cache coherence. If we reroute mid-request, we may need to rebuild KV for the new model or invalidate prefixes. That can blow up latency unless we budget for it.

danny: sales pressure is real. Two deals (~$multi-yr) will stall without a credible fallback+SLA story. We should aim parity for the immediate asks but design the API to enable richer policies later.

sara: sketch of plan: MVP parity: add `fallback_chain` field to route configs and implement synchronous hop-on-failure logic with conservative time budget; make guarantees explicit (only applies when dedicated/pinned capacity or best-effort otherwise). Differentiator: policy templates, cost/latency preview, and tenant-level soft-SLAs with crediting.

alex: propose concrete acceptance criteria for MVP: - API: allow `fallback_chain: [modelX, modelX-quant, modelY]` per-route or per-tenant. - Runtime: attempt models in order within a per-request timeout. - Bench: p95 end-to-end < 300ms on our medium-length benchmark workload. - No KV corruption, no silent prompt truncation.

julia: infra guardrails to add: - hard cap on fallback hops (<= 3) - per-request budget (default 600ms) enforced by router - telemetry: tag requests with hop index + sampled payload for postmortem.

mohit: model-quality risk: quant variants and smaller models will increase hallucination/accuracy regressions. Add an automated evaluation gate: fallback candidate must pass prompt-set thresholds (e.g., quality-degrade < 2.5%) or we mark it as "low-quality fallback" in response headers for client handling.

danny: need legal + sales input for SLA language. We need a rollback + incident playbook and explicit limits (e.g., SLO only for pinned clusters or dedicated nodes). Customers won't accept open-ended promises.

sara: timeline options: MVP parity = ~4w infra + 2w QA/docs; Differentiator (policy UX, simulations) = +82 weeks. Recommend shipping MVP this quarter and starting a spike for the richer UX next quarter.

alex: also add per-tenant opt-out and a kill-switch feature-flag for fast rollback. We'll require feature-flag gating and gradual rollout with detailed sampling.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: create FF `deterministic_fallback_v1`, add quota and sampling (`fallback_sample_rate=0.05`), add tracing hooks and metrics for hop counts, enable canary in us-west-2 first.

sara: owners: alex = API spec + PR for router changes; julia = guardrails/runbook + rollout plan; mohit = quality evals for quant and small models; danny = sales one-pager + legal SLA draft. I'll schedule a 30m sign-off on Friday. :calendar:

alex: opening spec PR today and will tag infra and mohit.

mohit: kicking off evals now, will publish a short report tomorrow with per-prompt deltas.

julia: drafting runbook and rollback steps; will include KV cache recovery options.

danny: prepping customer comms and will escalate to the two prospects.

sara: thanks team. Goal: ship MVP parity so we can close deals, and iterate on the differentiator (policy-first UX + simulated cost/latency) afterwards. :rocket:
